newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's Sharon met PLO official -report.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Sharon met PLO official -report.

text.p: Israel Television said on Friday hardline cabinet member Ariel Sharon met 10 days ago with senior PLO official Mahmoud Abbas.
Sharon has been one of the cabinet's fiercest opponents of peace deals with the PLO, branding Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat a "terrorist".

A spokesman for Sharon, tipped to become finance minister in Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's cabinet, said he did not know if the report was true. PLO officials were at a cabinet meeting and could not immediately be reached for comment.
The television said Abbas, better known as Abu Mazen, initiated the meeting which lasted several hours. The report did not say what the two men discussed.

Abbas, an architect of the landmark 1993 Israel-PLO peace deal, resigned last March as head of the Palestinian negotiating team over Israel's decision to withdraw troops from only small parts of the West Bank, contrary to the PLO's expectations.
That decision coupled with Israel's subsequent groundbreaking of a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem plunged peacemaking with the Palestine Liberation Organisation into crisis.
Sharon, a backer of Jewish settlement expansion in the West Bank and Gaza Strip, has demanded a seat on Netanyahu's three-member "kitchen cabinet" which directs Israeli peace moves.
Political analysts have said Foreign Minister David Levy and Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai oppose giving the hawkish ex-general a place in the inner team.
